system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for New York, United States. Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in New York itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent New York space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (Chelsea, Downtown, Uptown, Brooklyn/Queens, Hamptons) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several New York spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in New York, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: Gagosian
galleries.note: The benchmark global mega-gallery, with an unmatched blue-chip roster, extensive publishing operation and commanding fair and institutional presence.

galleries.name: David Zwirner
galleries.note: A globally dominant gallery known for museum-caliber exhibitions, major estates, influential publications and sustained artist development.

galleries.name: Hauser & Wirth
galleries.note: A multinational powerhouse combining major living artists and estates with ambitious exhibitions, research, publishing and institutional partnerships.

galleries.name: Pace Gallery
galleries.note: One of the longest-standing international leaders in postwar and contemporary art, with particular strength in abstraction, technology and experiential work.

galleries.name: Marian Goodman Gallery
galleries.note: A foundational conduit between European and American conceptual art, distinguished by an exceptionally rigorous, institutionally acclaimed program.

galleries.name: Gladstone Gallery
galleries.note: A highly influential gallery representing major figures across installation, film, sculpture and painting, with strong museum and biennial visibility.

galleries.name: Paula Cooper Gallery
galleries.note: A pioneering SoHo gallery whose enduring program helped define Minimalism, Conceptualism, performance and politically engaged contemporary art.

galleries.name: White Cube
galleries.note: The influential London-born gallery has a major New York base and a formidable international roster spanning YBA history and global contemporary art.

galleries.name: Lisson Gallery
galleries.note: A central force in Minimal, Conceptual and international contemporary art, backed by decades of influential artist relationships.

galleries.name: Matthew Marks Gallery
galleries.note: A selective, museum-oriented program uniting canonical postwar figures with critically important contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Lehmann Maupin
galleries.note: A major international gallery with longstanding strength in globally diverse, multidisciplinary and institutionally visible practices.

galleries.name: Perrotin
galleries.note: A high-profile global gallery whose expansive program bridges critically recognized contemporary art, popular culture and younger markets.

galleries.name: Jack Shainman Gallery
galleries.note: Long influential for championing Black, African and diasporic artists and supporting practices addressing race, history and social justice.

galleries.name: Luhring Augustine
galleries.note: A durable, critically respected gallery with a multigenerational roster and important roles in film, installation, sculpture and painting.

galleries.name: Sean Kelly
galleries.note: An internationally prominent program centered on conceptually rigorous artists, ambitious installations and strong institutional careers.

galleries.name: Sprüth Magers
galleries.note: A historically important European gallery with deep commitments to feminist, conceptual, photographic and media-based practices.

galleries.name: Petzel
galleries.note: A leading transatlantic gallery known for intellectually ambitious exhibitions and major artists from Europe and the United States.

galleries.name: 303 Gallery
galleries.note: A defining New York gallery since the 1980s, associated with influential developments in photography, video, installation and conceptual art.

galleries.name: Marianne Boesky Gallery
galleries.note: A major Chelsea gallery with a broad multigenerational program and a strong record of developing artists into institutional careers.

galleries.name: Tanya Bonakdar Gallery
galleries.note: Known for ambitious conceptual, installation, architectural and environmental practices with sustained museum and biennial recognition.

galleries.name: David Kordansky Gallery
galleries.note: The influential Los Angeles gallery's permanent New York space presents a prominent roster of painters, sculptors and interdisciplinary artists.

galleries.name: Greene Naftali
galleries.note: An intellectually exacting gallery closely identified with experimental, conceptually driven and critically influential contemporary art.

galleries.name: James Cohan
galleries.note: A substantial international program connecting established and emerging artists across painting, installation and socially engaged practices.

galleries.name: Karma
galleries.note: A highly influential gallery and publisher whose scholarship and exhibitions have helped reshape contemporary and postwar canons.

galleries.name: kurimanzutto
galleries.note: The Mexico City-founded gallery brings one of Latin America's most influential artist rosters and curatorial sensibilities to New York.

galleries.name: P·P·O·W
galleries.note: A longstanding leader in politically engaged, feminist and queer art, with important stewardship of major artists and estates.

galleries.name: Andrew Kreps Gallery
galleries.note: A critically respected gallery combining incisive emerging practices with historically important artists and estates.

galleries.name: Sikkema Malloy Jenkins
galleries.note: A deeply respected multigenerational program with particular strength in photography, painting and artists addressing identity and history.

galleries.name: Almine Rech
galleries.note: A major international gallery pairing prominent contemporary painters and sculptors with historically significant postwar artists.

galleries.name: Anton Kern Gallery
galleries.note: A tastemaking New York gallery with a strong record of building distinctive contemporary artists' careers over several decades.

galleries.name: Skarstedt
galleries.note: A powerful primary- and secondary-market gallery specializing in canonical postwar and contemporary artists and tightly curated exhibitions.

galleries.name: Kasmin
galleries.note: A prominent Chelsea gallery combining contemporary representation, major estates, public sculpture and strong postwar scholarship.

galleries.name: Galerie Lelong & Co.
galleries.note: A long-established gallery with notable commitments to women, Latin American artists and socially and environmentally engaged practices.

galleries.name: Tina Kim Gallery
galleries.note: An important international platform for Korean and diasporic artists, with strong scholarship and growing institutional influence.

galleries.name: Alexander Gray Associates
galleries.note: Known for rigorous historical recovery and advocacy for artists engaging politics, identity, feminism and social justice.

galleries.name: Bortolami
galleries.note: A critically regarded gallery recognized for adventurous programming, long-term artist support and influential off-site initiatives.

galleries.name: White Columns
galleries.note: New York's oldest alternative art space remains a crucial launchpad for emerging and underrecognized artists.

galleries.name: Artists Space
galleries.note: A foundational alternative institution whose experimental exhibitions, commissions and debates have shaped New York art since 1972.

galleries.name: Salon 94
galleries.note: A distinctive townhouse gallery known for close artist relationships and influential intersections among contemporary art, design and material culture.

galleries.name: Sperone Westwater
galleries.note: A historically important transatlantic gallery with deep roots in Conceptualism, Arte Povera and major contemporary painting and sculpture.

galleries.name: Lévy Gorvy Dayan
galleries.note: A high-level postwar and contemporary gallery distinguished by scholarly exhibitions, private-market reach and major institutional relationships.

galleries.name: Galerie Eva Presenhuber
galleries.note: A highly regarded European gallery with a New York program built around critically influential international artists.

galleries.name: Mariane Ibrahim
galleries.note: A fast-rising international gallery central to the market and institutional recognition of artists from Africa and its diaspora.

galleries.name: Mendes Wood DM
galleries.note: An influential Brazilian-founded gallery presenting a globally minded program with particular strength in Latin American art.

galleries.name: MASSIMODECARLO
galleries.note: A major international gallery whose New York space extends a prominent roster spanning established figures and market-leading younger artists.

galleries.name: Nara Roesler
galleries.note: One of Brazil's leading galleries, with significant strength in Latin American modern, conceptual and contemporary art.

galleries.name: Miles McEnery Gallery
galleries.note: A substantial Chelsea operation with a broad painting-centered program, major estates and consistent art-fair visibility.

galleries.name: Pilar Corrias
galleries.note: The London gallery's New York space presents an acclaimed international roster, with particular strength among women and moving-image artists.

galleries.name: Timothy Taylor
galleries.note: A respected transatlantic gallery pairing established postwar artists with critically and institutionally visible contemporary practices.

galleries.name: Galerie Buchholz
galleries.note: A highly influential, intellectually driven program associated with major conceptual, queer and interdisciplinary artists.

galleries.name: SculptureCenter
galleries.note: A leading commissioning institution for experimental sculpture and installation, with an exceptional record of identifying consequential artists early.

galleries.name: Swiss Institute
galleries.note: A globally oriented nonprofit presenting adventurous exhibitions, commissions and public programs by emerging and established artists.

galleries.name: The Kitchen
galleries.note: A foundational experimental venue whose interdisciplinary program has transformed performance, video, sound and visual art since 1971.

galleries.name: Anat Ebgi
galleries.note: An ascendant Los Angeles-founded gallery whose permanent New York space supports critically visible emerging and midcareer artists.

galleries.name: Miguel Abreu Gallery
galleries.note: A rigorous Lower East Side gallery and publishing enterprise associated with theory-driven art, film and intellectually demanding exhibitions.

galleries.name: Canada
galleries.note: A defining artist-founded gallery whose irreverent, community-based program helped shape downtown painting and sculpture.

galleries.name: Reena Spaulings Fine Art
galleries.note: An artist-run, conceptually agile gallery that has exerted unusual critical influence on downtown art and exhibition making.

galleries.name: 47 Canal
galleries.note: A tastemaking gallery known for introducing experimental artists working across technology, identity, installation and global cultural exchange.

galleries.name: Bridget Donahue
galleries.note: A critically admired gallery presenting formally adventurous, feminist and interdisciplinary work in focused exhibitions.

galleries.name: James Fuentes
galleries.note: An influential downtown gallery known for artist discovery, historical rediscovery and strong links to New York's cultural communities.

galleries.name: Garth Greenan Gallery
galleries.note: A scholarly gallery that has helped secure overdue recognition for important women, Indigenous artists and overlooked postwar figures.

galleries.name: Ortuzar Projects
galleries.note: A curatorial and research-led gallery acclaimed for historically incisive exhibitions and renewed attention to underrecognized artists.

galleries.name: Galerie Max Hetzler
galleries.note: One of Europe's most influential contemporary galleries, bringing a deep international roster and decades of market authority to New York.

galleries.name: GRIMM
galleries.note: An international gallery with a strong record of advancing younger painters and sculptors into museum and art-fair prominence.

galleries.name: Hales
galleries.note: A respected London-founded gallery with notable commitments to Black British art, interdisciplinary practices and important rediscoveries.

galleries.name: mor charpentier
galleries.note: An internationally minded gallery emphasizing politically engaged practices and artists from Latin America, Europe and the Middle East.

galleries.name: Acquavella Galleries
galleries.note: A venerable family gallery with exceptional secondary-market influence and selective representation of prominent contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Nahmad Contemporary
galleries.note: A powerful postwar and contemporary gallery known for ambitious historical juxtapositions and access to exceptional blue-chip material.

galleries.name: Venus Over Manhattan
galleries.note: Known for idiosyncratic, revisionist exhibitions that connect contemporary art with overlooked movements, vernacular culture and postwar history.

galleries.name: Luxembourg + Co.
galleries.note: A research-intensive gallery presenting museum-quality modern and contemporary exhibitions, often reconsidering established art-historical narratives.

galleries.name: kaufmann repetto
galleries.note: A respected Milan-founded gallery with an internationally diverse program and longstanding support for feminist and conceptually oriented practices.

galleries.name: Chapter NY
galleries.note: A closely watched gallery with a concise emerging program and a strong record of placing artists into institutional exhibitions.

galleries.name: Magenta Plains
galleries.note: A prominent downtown gallery combining emerging voices, midcareer development and productive reconsiderations of older artists.

galleries.name: Bureau
galleries.note: A critically influential gallery devoted to conceptually sharp, materially experimental and often institutionally ambitious practices.

galleries.name: Maxwell Graham
galleries.note: The successor to Essex Street maintains a highly regarded program of intellectually rigorous contemporary and historical exhibitions.

galleries.name: David Nolan Gallery
galleries.note: A longstanding gallery valued for serious drawing, European postwar art and thoughtful contemporary representation.

galleries.name: Rachel Uffner Gallery
galleries.note: A key Lower East Side gallery with a strong record of nurturing painters, sculptors and ceramic artists into wider recognition.

galleries.name: Nicelle Beauchene Gallery
galleries.note: A respected emerging and midcareer program known for measured artist development and materially inventive exhibitions.

galleries.name: Derek Eller Gallery
galleries.note: A durable downtown gallery with an independent sensibility and a strong multigenerational roster across drawing, painting and sculpture.

galleries.name: Klaus von Nichtssagend Gallery
galleries.note: A longstanding artist-centered gallery whose understated program has launched and sustained numerous critically respected careers.

galleries.name: Marc Straus
galleries.note: An expansive Lower East Side gallery presenting an international, multigenerational roster with particular strength in painting and sculpture.

galleries.name: Yossi Milo
galleries.note: An influential photography-centered gallery that has broadened into painting, sculpture and artists exploring identity and representation.

galleries.name: Company Gallery
galleries.note: A progressive downtown gallery particularly influential for queer, trans, digital and performance-oriented contemporary practices.

galleries.name: Lomex
galleries.note: A small but highly watched gallery known for unconventional exhibitions and artists circulating through New York's experimental scene.

galleries.name: Gordon Robichaux
galleries.note: An artist-run gallery acclaimed for intimate, research-rich exhibitions and advocacy for overlooked or unconventional practices.

galleries.name: Half Gallery
galleries.note: A compact but market-influential gallery recognized for identifying sought-after painters and staging energetic cross-generational exhibitions.

galleries.name: The Hole
galleries.note: A high-energy downtown gallery with substantial visibility for emerging painting, new media and art shaped by popular and internet culture.

galleries.name: Harper's
galleries.note: A rapidly expanded gallery with strong contemporary painting, publishing roots and an influential presence in both New York and the Hamptons.

galleries.name: Jeffrey Deitch
galleries.note: A veteran dealer and curator whose public-facing exhibitions connect contemporary art with street culture, fashion, performance and spectacle.

galleries.name: Michael Rosenfeld Gallery
galleries.note: An important scholarly gallery recognized for expanding the postwar canon and supporting major Black artists and estates.

galleries.name: Fergus McCaffrey
galleries.note: A research-oriented gallery with notable expertise in postwar Japanese art and materially radical American and European practices.

galleries.name: DC Moore Gallery
galleries.note: A longstanding American gallery with strong commitments to figurative art, abstraction, feminist histories and socially engaged practices.

galleries.name: Storefront for Art and Architecture
galleries.note: A globally influential experimental space commissioning exhibitions and projects at the intersection of contemporary art, architecture and public life.

galleries.name: apexart
galleries.note: A distinctive nonprofit known for open-call exhibitions, unconventional curatorial models and internationally networked public programming.

galleries.name: Participant Inc
galleries.note: A vital nonprofit platform for queer, feminist and politically challenging work that often falls outside commercial and institutional norms.

galleries.name: Smack Mellon
galleries.note: A major Brooklyn nonprofit offering ambitious exhibitions, commissions, studios and sustained support for underrepresented artists.

galleries.name: Amant
galleries.note: A well-resourced international arts organization presenting residencies, commissions, exhibitions and research across a substantial Brooklyn campus.

galleries.name: Pioneer Works
galleries.note: A prominent interdisciplinary nonprofit combining contemporary exhibitions with residencies, science, music, performance and publishing.

galleries.name: Recess
galleries.note: An artist-centered nonprofit recognized for process-based commissions, public engagement and the influential Assembly diversion program.

galleries.name: A.I.R. Gallery
galleries.note: A pioneering feminist, artist-run nonprofit founded in 1972, with enduring importance for women and nonbinary artists.
